questions.q: In scipy, stats.norm(loc=40, scale=5) describes a normal distribution. What do loc and scale represent?
options: loc is the standard deviation, scale is the mean
loc is the mean, scale is the variance
loc is the median, scale is the range
loc is the mean, scale is the standard deviation
questions.explain: loc is the mean and scale is the standard deviation, not the variance.

questions.q: Delivery times are normal with mean 40 and sd 5. Roughly what share of deliveries fall between 35 and 45 minutes?
questions.explain: 35 to 45 is within one standard deviation of the mean, which covers about 68% of a normal distribution.

questions.q: A delivery takes 52 minutes when the mean is 40 and sd is 5. What is its z-score?
questions.explain: z = (52 - 40) / 5 = 2.4, meaning 2.4 standard deviations above the mean.

questions.q: Which scipy method would you use to find the delivery time that 95% of deliveries beat (the 95th percentile)?
questions.explain: ppf is the inverse of the cdf: give it a probability and it returns the value below which that share of the distribution falls.

questions.q: You compute skewness for a sample and get 1.87. What is the most reasonable reading?
options: The data is strongly right-skewed, so treating it as normal is risky
Skewness is meaningless for continuous data
questions.explain: Normal data has skewness near 0. A value around 1.87 signals a long right tail, as in incomes or order values.
